decisions.decision: Frame the entire product as a novelty/publicity offer-and-selection experience, never as a real legal transfer of naming rights.
decisions.rationale: Naming rights to a child are not a transferable legal asset in any jurisdiction; claiming otherwise would be a false outcome claim.
rejected_alternatives: Building/wording it as an actual legal rights marketplace
constraints: All copy must disclaim non-binding, parents'-sole-discretion status before any offer/payment submission

decisions.decision: The single personal listing (MVP) is a hard requirement; the multi-user marketplace is a stretch goal that may be cut only if explicitly stated as cut.
decisions.rationale: Prompt hedges the marketplace with 'potentially' while the personal site is the stated primary ask; global rule prefers a smaller finished app over a larger half-built one.
rejected_alternatives: Treating both as equally hard requirements
Silently dropping the marketplace without disclosure
constraints: Any decision to cut the marketplace must be explicitly documented, not implied

decisions.decision: Checkout/payment is fully built end-to-end in the UI but settlement is simulated and clearly labeled demo/no real charge.
decisions.rationale: A live payment processor with real charges is a compliance/safety surface beyond what this build can own; simulated checkout still delivers the 'sell' experience.
rejected_alternatives: Wiring a real Stripe integration by default
Omitting checkout entirely
constraints: No flow may claim a real charge succeeded
Real Stripe-type integration only if user explicitly requests and confirms it later

decisions.decision: No screen may require real personal data about an actual minor; only placeholder-safe fields (due month/year, alias, short story) are collected.
decisions.rationale: This is UGC about children submitted by anonymous visitors — a magnet for abuse and a privacy risk if real child data is required.
rejected_alternatives: Collecting real child name/photo/birthdate fields
constraints: Applies to both the seed listing and any user-created listings

decisions.decision: Every listing and every offer must have a visible report/flag control with confirmation on use.
decisions.rationale: Anonymous UGC with bidding on children's names is an abuse magnet (offensive proposals, spam, impersonation); minimum moderation affordance is required even at MVP.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping without moderation controls and adding them later

decisions.decision: 'Great design' is operationalized as: full light/dark mode, no overlapping/clipped text (especially on the offers/leaderboard view), real empty/loading/success/error states, and no default unstyled form chrome.
decisions.rationale: The original phrase is unfalsifiable as written; it must cash out into checkable criteria per the global no-overlap and dark-mode rules.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'great design' as a subjective, unchecked aspiration
constraints: Verified in both light and dark mode, mobile and desktop widths

decisions.decision: Design the app around a single spiky share-session (link shared once, visited once), not a returning/habitual-use audience.
decisions.rationale: This is a novelty link product (baby-shower/group-chat/social share), not a service with organic repeat traffic; comparable gimmick/crowdfunding sites confirm this pattern.
rejected_alternatives: Designing for accounts/retention/repeat visits as a primary use case
constraints: Zero-to-value (understand + can participate) must work in well under a page-scroll's worth of content, front-loaded on the hero

decisions.decision: Adopt the crowdfunding-leaderboard pattern (hero item + public ranked contribution list + submission form + prominent disclaimer) as the structural model for the listing page.
decisions.rationale: This shape is well-established in comparable gimmick/crowdfunding products (GoFundMe donor lists, Kickstarter backer lists, 'name a star' sites) and matches the prompt_contract's required sorted public offers list.
rejected_alternatives: A novel/bespoke page structure without a comparable-pattern basis
constraints: Tone must read as playful/gift-economy, not auction-house/transactional, to avoid reading as creepy rather than charming

decisions.decision: Add a lightweight content filter (blocklist/length check) at submission time as part of MVP form validation, in addition to the already-contracted report/flag controls.
decisions.rationale: Anonymous UGC about a child on a public leaderboard is a high-probability abuse target; post-hoc reporting alone risks the first viral share being a screenshot of offensive content rather than the intended charming pitch.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on report/flag controls alone without submission-time filtering
constraints: Must not block legitimate playful submissions — filter for clearly abusive content, not aggressive false-positive blocking

decisions.decision: Treat the offers/leaderboard screen as the single highest-risk screen for visual QA, requiring explicit testing with long names, large dollar amounts, and long aliases together.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly the data-density + narrow-mobile-width combination that has caused overlapping-text failures elsewhere in this fleet's history.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the leaderboard as a standard list needing only default responsive styling
constraints: Must be verified with adversarial-length test data, not just short happy-path names/amounts, in both light/dark and mobile/desktop per DEC-prompt_contract-006

decisions.decision: Bake the non-binding/novelty disclaimer into the homepage hero headline copy itself, not only as a pre-submission footnote.
decisions.rationale: A screenshot shared out of context can crop out footnote-level disclaimers; putting the framing in the headline makes it survive lazy/partial screenshots and protects the reputational framing established in DEC-prompt_contract-001.
rejected_alternatives: Keeping the disclaimer solely at the pre-submission/checkout step as originally contracted
constraints: Does not replace the pre-submission disclaimer requirement (DEC-prompt_contract-001), it adds a second placement

decisions.decision: Treat this prompt as a single-app build, not a portfolio — one slug (monitizing-names), no sibling child projects, no portfolio-json manifest.
decisions.rationale: The prompt describes one product idea with one internally-hedged scope dimension (solo listing vs. multi-user platform), not a request for multiple independent apps across categories; splitting into siblings would invent unrequested structure.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting into separate 'personal-listing' and 'marketplace' sibling projects
constraints: No portfolio-json is emitted
build=true for the single selected app

decisions.decision: Flag now, explicitly, that the multi-user marketplace (create-listing + browse page) is the most likely component to be cut in a later build-scope phase, in favor of a fully polished single personal listing.
decisions.rationale: The prompt hedges the marketplace with 'potentially'; the actual target user (someone sent one specific family's link) gets little value from browsing strangers' listings; the standing contract already prefers a smaller finished app over a larger half-built one.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the marketplace as an equally-weighted hard requirement
Staying silent on cut-risk and letting a later phase discover/decide it unprompted
constraints: This does not finalize the cut — it must still be attempted if a later phase has capacity to do it without compromising the single listing's polish
If cut, DEC-prompt_contract-002's requirement to explicitly document the cut still applies

decisions.decision: Set the one-sentence product promise: a single page where one couple playfully sells naming rights to their future child via a sorted public offer list, a fake checkout, and headline-level framing that parents choose freely regardless of amount.
decisions.rationale: Converts the prompt and prior research/contract decisions into one concrete, buildable promise, satisfying the phase's required output.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the promise abstract/multi-sentence
constraints: Must remain consistent with DEC-prompt_contract-001's non-binding/novelty framing

decisions.decision: No accounts, login, or authentication anywhere in this build, for parents or visitors, now or for any future listing.
decisions.rationale: The scenario is a single spiky-session visitor reacting to a shared link; auth, an owner dashboard, and notification loops are scope creep that would turn a tight novelty page into a half-built platform.
rejected_alternatives: Adding a lightweight owner login for the parents to manage their listing
constraints: No screen may gate core functionality behind sign-in

decisions.decision: Cut the multi-user marketplace (create-your-own-listing + browse/discovery page) from this build; ship only the single personal listing.
decisions.rationale: Two phases already flagged this as likely-cut; a marketplace with no accounts, search, or discovery isn't a real platform, and the actual visitor persona (someone sent one specific link) has no use for browsing strangers' listings. Building it half-heartedly would weaken the one thing that makes this charming: it's personal and specific.
rejected_alternatives: Building a minimal create-listing + browse page alongside the personal listing
Deferring the cut decision to a later build-scope phase again
constraints: This decision itself is the explicit documentation of the cut required by DEC-prompt_contract-002
Marketplace remains a clean v2 candidate, not a cut-forever decision

decisions.decision: Sort the public offer list by amount descending with tiebreak by earliest submission; every offer's status is permanently 'open' with no close/decision/winner-announcement flow.
decisions.rationale: The prompt implies an ongoing, never-closing pitch, and there is no owner-facing surface in scope to drive a close/decide flow, since accounts and dashboards are explicitly cut.
rejected_alternatives: Adding a status field with open/closed/winner states
Leaving sort order and tie-breaking undefined for the design phase to improvise
constraints: Must be visually verified with tied-amount offers per DEC-product_research-004

decisions.decision: Implement report/flag as self-moderating: instant client-facing confirmation on report, and automatic hiding from the public list once an item crosses a small report threshold (three), with no human moderator in the loop.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-005 requires a working report/flag control, but there is no admin/moderator surface in scope (no accounts); a purely cosmetic 'thanks for reporting' with no effect would make the control non-functional in practice.
rejected_alternatives: Report control that only logs reports with no visible effect on the listed content
Building a moderator review queue/admin panel
constraints: Threshold and auto-hide behavior must be implemented, not just simulated in copy

decisions.decision: Apply a soft rate-limit on repeat offer submissions from the same visitor to prevent leaderboard spam, without blocking legitimate repeat joke offers entirely.
decisions.rationale: With no accounts, nothing else stops one visitor from submitting the same name/amount many times in a row and dominating the sorted list, undermining the leaderboard's credibility.
rejected_alternatives: No rate-limiting, allowing unlimited repeat submissions
Hard-blocking any second submission from the same session
constraints: Must not require an account or login to enforce

decisions.decision: Define paid value as the demo-checkout theater itself (real-time leaderboard reorder + fake receipt), not the offer submission alone — this is the product's reason to exist over a generic form.
decisions.rationale: Nothing else in the flow differentiates this from a Google Form/GoFundMe/spreadsheet; the transactional feeling is the entire wedge.
rejected_alternatives: Treating checkout as pure compliance theater with no design priority
Leaving paid value undefined and letting design phases guess
constraints: Checkout UX must prioritize the instant/satisfying transactional feeling above all other polish

decisions.decision: Define subscription as a device-local 'Patron' pass (localStorage entitlement, demo-charged, no account) unlocking: rate-limit exemption, edit/withdraw own offer within a window, and a persistent leaderboard badge.
decisions.rationale: No-accounts rule (DEC-initial_discussion-002) rules out server-side subscription tiers; the phase requires subscription value to be functional, not cosmetic.
rejected_alternatives: Cosmetic-only subscription (badge with no functional unlock)
Server-side account-backed subscription tier
constraints: Copy must never claim this is a durable/permanent purchase — it is explicitly device/session-scoped and lost on storage clear or device switch

decisions.decision: The public offer list requires a real shared backend/store from v1, not a deferred cloud path — it cannot be local-first since it is inherently shared multi-visitor data.
decisions.rationale: Corrects an implicit assumption risk: 'local-first' cannot apply to data whose entire value is being seen identically by every visitor.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring the shared list to a 'future cloud path' as originally implied by the phase framing
constraints: Cloud/shared store is a v1 dependency for the offer list specifically, not optional

decisions.decision: Scope local-first behavior narrowly to: Patron entitlement, visitor's own rate-limit counter, an offline submission queue with a distinct 'queued' state, and a last-seen-offers snapshot for return-visit comparison.
decisions.rationale: These are the only pieces of state that are genuinely single-device and don't require coordination with other visitors.
rejected_alternatives: Applying local-first framing broadly across the whole app
constraints: Offline queue must never show a false success/confirmation state — only 'queued, will send when back online'

decisions.decision: Define the viral/growth mechanism as a post-submission personal shareable result card (rank + brag line) plus a return-visit 'you've been outbid' comparison against the local last-seen snapshot.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the phase's required viral/niche growth angle without any accounts, email, or push infrastructure, consistent with the no-accounts constraint.
rejected_alternatives: Email/push notification-based re-engagement (requires accounts/infra explicitly out of scope)
No growth mechanism beyond the initial share
constraints: Share card must be personal/dynamic (actual rank), not generic marketing copy

decisions.decision: Require a per-device one-report-per-item cap on the report/flag control, in addition to the existing 3-report auto-hide threshold.
decisions.rationale: Without a per-device cap, one person can trigger auto-hide alone via multiple tabs/reloads, making the self-moderating design from DEC-initial_discussion-005 non-functional against trivial gaming.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the report threshold uncapped per device
constraints: Must be enforced the same way as the submission rate-limit (device-local, no account)

decisions.decision: Sort tiebreaks must use a server-assigned persistence timestamp, not client-submitted time, to keep ordering deterministic under concurrent submissions.
decisions.rationale: A shared link going viral in a group chat makes near-simultaneous submissions realistic; client-time tiebreaks could cause the leaderboard to re-sort unpredictably on refresh, undermining trust in the list.
rejected_alternatives: Using client-submitted timestamps for tiebreak ordering
constraints: Refines, does not replace, the amount-descending/earliest-submission sort rule from DEC-initial_discussion-004

decisions.decision: Define the MVP slice as the single end-to-end loop: hero → seed listing → sorted offer list → offer form → content filter → disclaimer → demo checkout → persisted confirmation → list reorder.
decisions.rationale: Prior phases accumulated many features (Patron pass, offline queue, outbid comparison, share cards); this phase's job is to isolate the one workflow that must be flawless, not let the full feature list count as 'small'.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the full per_app_product_brief feature set as the MVP slice
constraints: This loop must be built end-to-end with zero dead ends before any deferred feature is added

decisions.decision: Treat the checkout-completion moment (real-time leaderboard reorder + fake receipt) as the single highest-leverage design investment in the app, to be protected over other polish.
decisions.rationale: If that moment doesn't feel like a real, slightly absurd transaction, the app is just a form with extra steps and the core wedge from per_app_product_brief (DEC-per_app_product_brief-001) falls flat.
rejected_alternatives: Treating checkout confirmation as a generic success toast/state
constraints: Must include a visible reorder animation and a receipt-styled confirmation, not a plain success message

decisions.decision: Sequence the Patron pass, offline submission queue, and last-seen-offers outbid comparison out of the first build — deferred to a later slice, not deleted.
decisions.rationale: All three mechanisms only deliver value to a returning visitor, but the established modal user (DEC-product_research-001) is single-session; building three return-visit features before the first-time-visitor loop is proven would misallocate the smallest-slice effort.
rejected_alternatives: Including all per_app_product_brief features in the first build
Silently dropping these features without stating it as a sequencing decision
constraints: Must be stated explicitly as sequencing/deferral, not scope deletion, per the same discipline applied to the marketplace cut (DEC-initial_discussion-003)
If a later phase decides to cut these permanently, that must be documented explicitly, not implied

decisions.decision: Keep the post-submission shareable result card (rank + brag line) in scope for the first build, unlike the other deferred growth/retention features.
decisions.rationale: Unlike the Patron pass, offline queue, and outbid comparison, the share card is cheap (a styled summary of data already collected) and its payoff happens within the same single session, matching the established modal user.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring the share card alongside the other return-visit-dependent features

decisions.decision: Treat the content filter and report/flag auto-hide as safety-load-bearing requirements of this same MVP slice, not deferrable polish.
decisions.rationale: These are the only moderation affordances in a build with no admin surface (DEC-initial_discussion-005, DEC-product_research-003); shipping the submission loop without them would leave anonymous UGC about a child unmoderated at first launch.
rejected_alternatives: Treating content filtering/moderation as a post-MVP polish pass
constraints: Must be functionally live (not simulated in copy) in the first build

decisions.decision: Design the zero-offer empty state as part of this same MVP slice, since it is the first state every real visitor will encounter before any offers exist.
decisions.rationale: A freshly launched listing has zero offers by definition; an undesigned empty state would be the actual first impression of the product, contradicting the standing empty-state design rule (DEC-prompt_contract-006).
rejected_alternatives: Treating the empty state as a later polish pass after seed data exists

decisions.decision: Treat report/flag auto-hide as a soft, gameable deterrent rather than real moderation: document it as an accepted limitation, mitigate by soft-removing (not hard-deleting) auto-hidden offers from the public list, and require copy that never oversells its robustness.
decisions.rationale: With no accounts, a determined actor can trivially defeat the per-device report cap via incognito/multiple devices; treating it as solved would misrepresent moderation strength to visitors.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the per-device report cap as a solved/robust moderation system
Hard-deleting auto-hidden offers from the store
constraints: Auto-hidden offers must remain recoverable in the data store, not hard-deleted
Reporting UI copy must not claim strong moderation guarantees

decisions.decision: Treat the soft submission rate-limit as friction against casual spam only, not a security control — nothing downstream may assume it caps a determined actor using private browsing or multiple devices.
decisions.rationale: A device/localStorage-based rate-limit is trivially defeated by an incognito window; overstating its guarantees would be a false design assumption carried into build.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming the rate-limit reliably prevents leaderboard spam from a determined actor

decisions.decision: The demo checkout must never present a functional field capable of accepting real payment data (card number, CVV, etc.) — all checkout fields must be non-functional decoration, pre-filled with obviously-fake data, or structurally incapable of accepting a real PAN.
decisions.rationale: A checkout convincing enough to deliver the required 'real transaction' feeling (DEC-per_app_product_brief-001) is also convincing enough that an inattentive visitor could attempt to enter real financial data, creating an unwanted PCI/compliance exposure with no posture to handle it.
rejected_alternatives: Building a realistic-looking but technically functional payment form with client-side-only validation
Leaving this as an implementation detail for the build phase to improvise
constraints: No checkout field may structurally accept a real 16-digit card number or CVV
This constraint is safety-load-bearing, not a style preference, and may not be silently dropped

decisions.decision: Offer amount requires an explicit reasonable maximum (approximately $10,000,000) and must reject negative, zero, and non-numeric input; alias and story fields require explicit character caps.
decisions.rationale: Unbounded numeric/text input will eventually produce adversarial-length values that break the offers/leaderboard layout, which prior phases already flagged as the highest visual-QA-risk screen.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving amount/alias/story fields unbounded and relying on layout CSS alone to absorb any length
constraints: Exact cap values may be tuned during design/build but caps themselves are mandatory, not optional

decisions.decision: The submission-time content filter must return an actionable, specific rejection reason rather than a generic 'rejected' response.
decisions.rationale: A generic silent rejection on a false positive (e.g., a legitimate non-English name with diacritics/apostrophes) reads to the visitor as the site being broken, causing bounce.
rejected_alternatives: Generic 'submission rejected' messaging with no reason given
constraints: Applies to all content-filter rejections, not just the abusive-content case

decisions.decision: Require a distinct, tested error state for the case where the checkout animation completes visually but the backend persistence write fails — the UI must never let the success/reorder spectacle finish and then reveal failure after the fact, and must provide a clear retry action.
decisions.rationale: Allowing a completed success animation to later be contradicted by a failed write is exactly the 'claims an outcome that hasn't happened' violation the global rules forbid, and directly threatens the confirmation-only-after-persisted requirement (DEC-prompt_contract testable requirement 3).
rejected_alternatives: Assuming persistence failures are rare enough not to need an explicit UI path
Showing the success animation optimistically before persistence confirms
constraints: Must be verified by actually killing the network mid-submission during testing, not just assumed correct

decisions.decision: No passively-collected visitor data (IP address, user agent, or similar) may ever be logged, displayed, or exported anywhere in the product; the owner's own consensual disclosure of due-month/year in the seed listing is unaffected by this rule and does not violate DEC-prompt_contract-004.
decisions.rationale: Anonymous UGC submission must mean anonymous end-to-end, not just on the visible surface; distinguishing owner self-disclosure (consent) from third-party visitor data collection (no consent) prevents this rule from being misapplied to the seed listing itself.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving passive data handling unspecified and letting a build phase decide informally
constraints: Applies to current UI and any future export/reporting feature

decisions.decision: The leaderboard reorder animation must include an aria-live announcement of the rank/position change in addition to the visual transition.
decisions.rationale: Multiple prior phases named this animation the single highest-leverage design moment in the app; without an aria-live announcement, that moment is entirely invisible to screen-reader users, which is an accessibility floor failure.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the reorder moment as purely visual with no accessible equivalent

decisions.decision: Finalize the MoSCoW split: must-haves are exactly the next_steps_small MVP loop plus every safety/edge-case item detailed_discussion marked non-negotiable (22 numbered items); should/could is the shareable result card and cosmetic polish; won't-build is the marketplace, accounts, Patron pass, offline queue, outbid comparison, and any human moderation surface.
decisions.rationale: This phase's job is prioritization, not re-opening product debate; every item traces to an already-locked decision from prior phases.
rejected_alternatives: Re-litigating already-decided scope
Treating the full accumulated feature backlog as all must-have
constraints: requirements-json in this phase's output is the machine contract the adherence gate grades against

decisions.decision: Downgrade the post-submission shareable result card from a must-have interaction (as next_steps_small framed it) to should/could.
decisions.rationale: It's a real but optional growth lever; if build pressure forces a tradeoff, it should be the card's polish that gives, not any safety-load-bearing behavior (payment-field safety, failed-persistence error state, report/flag auto-hide, content filter).
rejected_alternatives: Keeping it as a must-have per next_steps_small's original framing
Cutting it entirely
constraints: Must be built if time allows within the must-have list being fully done first
This is a priority-tier change, stated explicitly, not a silent scope cut

decisions.decision: Compound requirements (confirmation-only-after-persisted; report/flag) must be split into separate numbered, independently-testable requirement line items rather than left as single bullets with implied sub-behaviors.
decisions.rationale: A single flattened bullet lets a build phase claim done after shipping only the happy path or only the confirmation half of report/flag, silently missing the failure-path or cap/threshold behaviors.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these as single compound bullets in the requirements-json
constraints: Applies specifically to the confirmation/error-state pair and the report-confirm/per-device-cap/auto-hide triad

decisions.decision: Commit to concrete adversarial-length test values for the offers list stress test: a 60-character alias, three offers tied at the same amount, and one offer at $9,999,999.
decisions.rationale: "Adversarial-length data" has been called critical by three prior phases without ever being pinned to actual numbers, risking inconsistent interpretation by whoever tests it.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the adversarial test data undefined for a later phase to interpret
constraints: These exact values must be used in visual QA for the offers list, in both light and dark mode

decisions.decision: Explicitly state, in the won't-build list, that no server-side moderation queue or human review/admin surface will be built — the self-moderating auto-hide mechanism is the entire moderation story for this build.
decisions.rationale: "Report/flag control" as a bare phrase could otherwise be built by a later phase as if it needs an admin backend, contradicting the no-accounts constraint and inflating scope.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving this unstated and letting a build phase infer or guess

decisions.decision: Adopt 'Delivery-Room Trading Floor' as the named design language: a warm pastel/nursery aesthetic fused with stock-ticker/scoreboard kinetic vocabulary (bold numerals, rank badges, spring-physics reorder motion).
decisions.rationale: Executes the standing playful/gift-economy-not-auction-house tone rule (DEC-product_research-002) by fusing, rather than choosing between, the product's two literal halves — a birth announcement and a live dollar leaderboard.
rejected_alternatives: A single-metaphor design (pure nursery/baby-shower aesthetic with no leaderboard energy)
A pure fintech/trading-floor aesthetic with no warmth
Generic 'clean and modern' styling
constraints: Palette and iconography must read as specific to this app, not swappable with another app's theme

decisions.decision: Set the emotional target as: the visitor feels like they crashed a fun, slightly absurd party game and their offer physically moved a shared scoreboard — delighted and a little smug, never like they filled out a form or transacted with a stranger.
decisions.rationale: Gives every downstream styling and motion decision a concrete emotional bar to be checked against.
rejected_alternatives: A more transactional/serious emotional target matching a real marketplace

decisions.decision: Specify the signature interaction concretely: demo-pay tap → checkout sheet flips into a stamped carnival-ticket receipt → sheet dismisses → leaderboard cards spring-reflow with the visitor's own card glowing in its new slot → aria-live announces the new rank instantly.
decisions.rationale: Multiple prior phases named this the single highest-leverage screen but left it abstract; this phase turns it into a buildable spec rather than leaving it for a build phase to improvise under pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the reorder/receipt moment as an unspecified 'nice animation' for the build phase to invent
constraints: Must include a stamped/receipt-styled visual object, spring-physics reorder motion, a glow/pulse on the visitor's own card, and an aria-live rank announcement per R-013/R-014

decisions.decision: Explicitly reject the generic default UI (plain stacked list rows, stock browser form chrome, green success toast) and name four concrete differences: ranked cards vs. table rows, spring re-sort vs. instant snap, styled sheets vs. raw browser chrome, receipt-object vs. toast.
decisions.rationale: Phase playbook requires naming and rejecting the default-looking version with concrete differences, not adjectives.
rejected_alternatives: Describing the design only in positive terms without naming what's being avoided

decisions.decision: Lock the screen inventory to: single long-scroll home (hero+disclaimer, story block, leaderboard, sticky mobile CTA), offer-submission sheet, checkout sheet, reorder/receipt success state, distinct checkout-failure/retry state, report-confirmation micro-states, and a dedicated zero-offer empty state for the leaderboard.
decisions.rationale: Matches the single-listing, no-accounts, no-marketplace scope already locked by prior phases while giving every required state (R-011, R-012, R-020) an explicit screen home.
rejected_alternatives: Adding additional pages/screens beyond the single-listing scope
constraints: No screen beyond this inventory is needed or expected for MVP

decisions.decision: Define explicit per-surface state models: leaderboard (loading/empty/populated/reordering, with soft-hidden reported offers simply not rendering), form (idle/inline-validating/content-filter-rejected-with-reason/valid-ready), checkout (idle/processing/success/distinct failure-retry), report controls (idle-flag/instant-confirmed/already-reported-this-device-disabled).
decisions.rationale: Phase playbook requires a state model per screen, not vague UX language; also operationalizes several already-locked requirements (R-007, R-011, R-012, R-017) into concrete UI states.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving states implicit/undocumented for the build phase to infer

decisions.decision: Restrict pastel colors to accents only (badges, confetti, card edges); body text and all dollar amounts always render in high-contrast ink/near-black or near-white, verified in both light and dark mode.
decisions.rationale: A pastel-heavy nursery palette risks silently failing WCAG contrast, especially in dark mode, if not scoped now — pre-resolving this avoids discovering it during visual QA.
rejected_alternatives: Applying pastel tones broadly to body text and amounts
Deferring the contrast decision to the build/QA phase
constraints: Must be verified against both light and dark backgrounds per the standing dark-mode rule

decisions.decision: Require focus trapping and return-focus on both sheets (offer form, checkout), and real accessible labels on every checkout field even though those fields are functionally decorative/non-functional.
decisions.rationale: A screen-reader user must understand the checkout is a deliberate fake 'tap to confirm,' not a broken or silently-missing real payment form; this closes an accessibility gap the payment-safety rule (DEC-detailed_discussion-003) could otherwise create.
rejected_alternatives: Treating decorative checkout fields as exempt from accessible labeling since they're not functionally real

decisions.decision: Model the submission flow as an explicit state machine — idle → validating → filter-checking → filter-rejected(reason) → ready → disclaimer-ack → checkout-processing → [persist write resolves] → success(receipt+reorder+aria-live) OR failure(retry, data preserved) — where the reorder animation is the render effect of the persisted/server-echoed offer list, never a client-side splice-and-hope.
decisions.rationale: R-011 (confirm only after persistence), R-012 (distinct failure state that must never appear after a completed success animation), R-013 (visibly animated reorder), and R-014 (instant aria-live) all compete for the same few seconds of UI; only an explicit, network-gated state machine lets all four coexist without risking the exact false-outcome bug the project has guarded against since detailed_discussion.
rejected_alternatives: Treating processing→success as a CSS transition triggered on button-tap (optimistic UI)
Client-side re-sorting the list instead of rendering the server's returned order
constraints: Reorder animation must be driven by the persisted/refetched offer list, not invented client-side
Also resolves R-003's tiebreak requirement: the client renders whatever order the server returns using its own timestamp, never invents order

decisions.decision: Lock concrete design tokens as the canonical spec: type scale (Display 40/44 through Caption 12/16, plus a distinct 24/28 rank numeral), 8pt spacing grid with steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64, corner radii (8/16/24/999), and full light+dark hex values for every semantic color role.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires explicit values everywhere so a builder invents nothing; three prior phases promised light/dark and responsive rigor without ever supplying numbers.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving tokens as adjectives ('warm pastel', 'rounded') for the build phase to interpret
constraints: Pastel tones (accent-pink) restricted to accents only, never body text or dollar amounts, per DEC-design_discussion-007

decisions.decision: Specify the checkout card field as a non-editable, pre-rendered visual (e.g. static '•••• •••• •••• 4242, DEMO/DEMO') rather than a text input styled to look like a card field.
decisions.rationale: A structural guarantee (can't be an input at all) is stronger than validation-based prevention of real PAN entry, directly strengthening the payment-safety rule from detailed_discussion.
rejected_alternatives: A styled text `<input>` with client-side validation rejecting real-looking card numbers
constraints: Must still carry a real accessible label per DEC-design_discussion-008

decisions.decision: Specify the reorder motion implementation concretely: FLIP-style position diffing, ~420ms spring-like ease (cubic-bezier(0.34,1.3,0.64,1)), glow/pulse on the visitor's own card; on prefers-reduced-motion, skip the position tween and glow but keep the aria-live announcement plus a simple opacity/highlight flash.
decisions.rationale: 'Spring physics' as named in design_discussion needed an actual web-buildable implementation note, and the accessibility requirement (aria-live) must survive independent of whether motion is enabled.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the reduced-motion case unspecified
A naive re-rendered sort without position diffing (cards would teleport instead of reflow)

decisions.decision: Require CI-enforced contrast checks (e.g. axe or a contrast lint script) for every light/dark color pairing rather than a manual visual pass.
decisions.rationale: "Verified in both modes" has been promised by three prior phases without anyone naming the verification mechanism; a pastel-adjacent palette is exactly the kind of thing that quietly fails WCAG contrast if only checked by eye.
rejected_alternatives: Manual visual QA pass only

decisions.decision: localStorage-backed features (submission rate-limit, per-device report cap) must degrade silently when storage is unavailable (e.g. Safari private browsing, blocking extensions) — omit the dependent UI state rather than throw or block.
decisions.rationale: These are soft, best-effort mechanisms per detailed_discussion's own framing; a hard failure on a first mobile share (the most likely entry point) would be a worse outcome than simply not showing the 'already reported' state.
rejected_alternatives: Letting a missing localStorage throw/crash the relevant component
Blocking the action entirely when storage is unavailable

decisions.decision: The seed listing's content must be present in the initial HTML response (server-rendered or statically generated), not fetched client-side after a blank first paint.
decisions.rationale: This is the concrete implementation path for R-001 actually passing on a cold mobile load; the fleet's own anti-pattern log repeatedly flags blank-screen-then-content as a visual QA failure.
rejected_alternatives: Client-side fetch-after-mount with a loading spinner on first paint

decisions.decision: Skip pausing for external Claude Design; hand the spec directly to the build phase, while still providing a fallback prompt for optionality.
decisions.rationale: Every token, component, and state is concrete enough for a builder to write a theme file and component library directly, and the app's small surface (one page, two sheets) doesn't benefit from an external handoff seam.
rejected_alternatives: Pausing the run for an external Claude Design pass

decisions.decision: Confirm this build remains a web app; decline to produce a SwiftUI/StoreKit/native-iOS architecture, since no phase has ever decided to pivot platforms and doing so here would silently override ~40 locked web-specific decisions.
decisions.rationale: The original prompt explicitly requested a web app, and every phase since (product_research, per_app_product_brief, design_discussion, design_handoff) built out web-specific mechanics (localStorage, aria-live, SSR first paint, shared HTTP backend) that have no native equivalent without a full re-decision.
rejected_alternatives: Producing a from-scratch SwiftUI architecture recommendation as though this were a native build
Silently treating the phase as not applicable with no output
constraints: Tech_specs proceeds with a standard web stack, not a Swift/Xcode target
Any future native iOS build is a new, unscoped v2 decision requiring its own product/design pass

decisions.decision: Document the report/flag per-device cap and the submission rate-limit as session-scoped, not device-scoped, and require QA to test the 'storage silently cleared, item becomes reportable/submittable again' path.
decisions.rationale: Safari's Intelligent Tracking Prevention can clear localStorage in ~7 days even outside private browsing, independent of any adversarial user action — a distinct failure mode from the 'storage unavailable at all' case already covered by DEC-design_handoff-006.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Safari storage volatility as covered by the existing 'degrade silently when storage unavailable' rule
Leaving this edge case undiscovered until real-world QA
constraints: Copy must never imply a longer-than-session guarantee for either mechanism
QA must explicitly test the cleared-storage-then-resubmit path, not just storage-never-available

decisions.decision: Record, as a standing non-blocking note, that a future WKWebView wrapper of this app for App Store distribution would likely be rejected under Guideline 4.2, and that any real native iOS build requires its own scoped redesign of subscription, persistence, and the no-accounts rule.
decisions.rationale: Naming this risk once now is cheaper than rediscovering it mid-build in a future phase; it does not block or alter the current web build.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving this risk undocumented for a future phase to discover the hard way
constraints: Does not commit the project to any native build; informational only

decisions.decision: Adopt Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) on a Node.js runtime (not edge) as the web framework.
decisions.rationale: React Server Components deliver the seed listing in the initial HTML response for free, satisfying DEC-design_handoff-007's SSR-first-paint requirement without hand-rolled SSR, and a Node runtime supports a real embedded SQLite file.
rejected_alternatives: Edge runtime
Client-fetch-after-mount SPA
Separate frontend + backend service split

decisions.decision: Use embedded SQLite (better-sqlite3, WAL mode) as the persistence layer for the shared Listing, Offer, and Report data.
decisions.rationale: This is a single-listing, single-writer-workload app; SQLite's serialized writes make the server-assigned-timestamp tiebreak (DEC-per_app_product_brief-007) correct without explicit locking, and satisfies DEC-per_app_product_brief-003's requirement for a real shared store from v1.
rejected_alternatives: Hosted Postgres (unneeded operational overhead at this scale)
In-memory-only store (violates the real-persistence requirement)

decisions.decision: Style with Tailwind CSS v4, declaring the full design_handoff token set (type scale, 8pt spacing, light/dark color roles, corner radii) once in an @theme block, referenced everywhere.
decisions.rationale: Matches the standing 'no hardcoded font/color literals' rule and gives every component the same canonical token source.
rejected_alternatives: CSS-in-JS
Hand-rolled CSS modules with literal values

decisions.decision: Hand-roll the FLIP reorder animation using the native Web Animations API instead of a third-party motion library.
decisions.rationale: The curve, duration, and reduced-motion behavior are already fully specified in design_handoff; a small hand-rolled implementation avoids a dependency that could silently mishandle prefers-reduced-motion.
rejected_alternatives: Framer Motion or similar animation library

decisions.decision: Add ambient polling of GET /api/offers (~20s interval, paused via Page Visibility API when backgrounded) so the leaderboard also animates in response to other visitors' submissions, not only the viewer's own.
decisions.rationale: Strengthens the 'alive scoreboard' emotional target (DEC-design_discussion-002) at low cost by reusing the same FLIP diff/animation code already required for self-submissions.
rejected_alternatives: No ambient updates — static list until the visitor personally submits
WebSocket/SSE push infrastructure
constraints: Scoped as should-have; must never take build priority over safety-load-bearing behaviors per DEC-app_features-002

decisions.decision: Add a server-side anonymous session token (random httpOnly cookie, crypto.randomUUID(), not derived from IP/UA) used to enforce the same soft rate-limit and one-report-per-item cap on the server, not just in client localStorage.
decisions.rationale: Every abuse-prevention mechanism locked through detailed_discussion lived only in client localStorage, which does nothing to stop a script POSTing directly to the API; this closes that gap without accounts or passive data collection.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving enforcement entirely client-side
Deriving the token from IP/user-agent (would violate the passive-data-collection ban)
Real accounts/login (violates the no-accounts rule)
constraints: Token must never be displayed or exported anywhere
Remains a soft, cookie-clearing-gameable mechanism — accepted limitation, not a security guarantee, consistent with DEC-detailed_discussion-001/002

decisions.decision: Model offer amounts as integer cents (never float) throughout the data layer and API.
decisions.rationale: Keeps sorting and display exact at adversarial values like $9,999,999, avoiding floating-point rounding artifacts on the highest-risk screen.
rejected_alternatives: Floating-point dollar amounts

decisions.decision: Implement report/flag auto-hide as a soft delete via a nullable hiddenAt column plus reportCount, filtering hidden rows out of public queries; rows are never hard-deleted.
decisions.rationale: Directly implements DEC-detailed_discussion-001's requirement that auto-hidden offers remain recoverable, not destroyed.
rejected_alternatives: Hard-deleting auto-hidden offers

decisions.decision: Pin four non-negotiable test classes tied to this project's specific named risks: content-filter abusive-vs-legitimate-non-English unit tests, a persistence-failure-after-successful-animation API test, a Playwright pass using the exact pinned adversarial values (60-char alias, three tied amounts, $9,999,999) in light/dark and mobile/desktop, and a cleared-localStorage-mid-session report-reset test.
decisions.rationale: Generic test coverage would not specifically catch the failure modes nine prior phases named by ID; each test maps directly to a locked requirement or decision.
rejected_alternatives: Generic/unscoped test coverage left to the build phase to interpret

decisions.decision: Lock the deploy target to a single long-lived Node process on a persistent-writable-disk host (e.g. Fly.io/Render/Railway/VPS-style), explicitly excluding serverless/edge platforms, as milestone zero before any schema work.
decisions.rationale: DEC-tech_specs-002's embedded SQLite choice is only valid on a host with a persistent filesystem and a long-lived process; a serverless/edge deploy would silently break the 'real shared backend from v1' requirement by losing or diverging the SQLite file between invocations.
rejected_alternatives: Deploying to a serverless/edge platform and discovering the SQLite failure mode after build
Silently swapping to a hosted DB without flagging the change to DEC-tech_specs-002
constraints: No schema/data-layer work begins until the deploy target is confirmed to provide persistent disk + single long-running process

decisions.decision: Sequence the build into 8 dependency-ordered milestones: deploy-target lock, data layer, service layer, API layer (against real services, no stubs), core submission-loop UI + state machine, signature interaction polish, should-have additions, cross-cutting QA + final verification.
decisions.rationale: The interfaces-json from tech_specs implies a real dependency chain (data → services → API → UI → polish) that isn't obviously ordered as a flat feature list; sequencing it prevents UI work from starting against mocked APIs and prevents polish from competing with safety-load-bearing work.
rejected_alternatives: Building UI and backend in parallel against mocked endpoints
Treating the full feature set as one undifferentiated milestone
constraints: UI milestones may not begin against stubbed/mocked API responses
Polish (milestone 6) and should-have work (milestone 7) are strictly gated behind the core loop (milestone 5) being fully tested

decisions.decision: Pin the submission rate-limit threshold to a concrete value: max 5 offers per 10 minutes per session, enforced identically client-side (localStorage) and server-side (AnonSession cookie).
decisions.rationale: Tech_specs specified the RateLimitResult shape but never a threshold, risking an arbitrary unreviewed number being picked mid-implementation by whoever writes rate-limit.ts.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the threshold undefined for the build phase to pick informally
constraints: Remains a soft, gameable friction mechanism per DEC-detailed_discussion-002, not a security control

decisions.decision: Require the four tech_specs-pinned test classes plus a new concurrent-submission tiebreak test to be built in the same milestone as the feature they verify, never deferred to a final QA pass.
decisions.rationale: Tests swept to the end become negotiable under time pressure; each of these five tests maps directly to a previously-named failure mode this project has worried about across multiple phases.
rejected_alternatives: Bundling all testing into a final QA/polish milestone
constraints: The concurrent-submission test (two offers posted at effectively the same millisecond) must confirm SQLite's single-writer serialization actually produces the deterministic tiebreak order DEC-per_app_product_brief-007 requires, not just assume it

decisions.decision: Gate the ambient polling should-have feature (DEC-tech_specs-005) behind full completion and testing of the core submission state machine, with an explicit required check that a poll-triggered reorder never fires during an in-progress local submission.
decisions.rationale: A poll that reorders the list out from under someone actively filling out the offer form would be a real regression, and this interaction has not been UX-validated by any prior phase.
rejected_alternatives: Building ambient polling alongside core submission work with no interaction check
constraints: Ambient polling must not be enabled until milestones 5 and 6 are stable and tested

decisions.decision: Require the CI-enforced contrast lint (DEC-design_handoff-005) to be actually wired into CI before any screen is marked visually verified, rather than treating the decision-log promise as sufficient.
decisions.rationale: Three prior phases promised light/dark contrast verification without naming the enforcement mechanism; a decision-log entry alone doesn't run a check.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the CI lint as done once specified in design_handoff without confirming it's actually running

decisions.decision: Root the Next.js project directly in .agent_cwd (no monorepo nesting), matching tech_specs' file/module layout exactly.
decisions.rationale: This session is scoped to write only inside .agent_cwd, and tech_specs already specified the full app/, components/, lib/, hooks/, types/, tests/, scripts/ layout at a project root — adding indirection would serve no purpose.
rejected_alternatives: Nesting the app under a subdirectory or monorepo package structure

decisions.decision: Assign file ownership by the four tech_specs interface lanes (data_domain, services_utilities, primary_ui, polish_resilience) and treat that ownership map, not git branching, as the conflict-prevention mechanism.
decisions.rationale: The interfaces-json already tagged every type/function with an owning lane; turning that into file ownership is direct and requires no new structure, and branch-per-lane would add merge overhead with no benefit in one shared working directory.
rejected_alternatives: Branching per lane
Leaving file ownership implicit/undocumented
constraints: Shared files (package.json, tsconfig.json) take additive-only diffs, flagged by whichever lane touches them

decisions.decision: Allow primary_ui to build presentational component shells (cards, sheets, empty states) against static fixture props in parallel with data/service-layer work, but forbid wiring real fetch calls or the useOfferSubmission state machine until the API layer (T-009) is complete.
decisions.rationale: Project_plan's 'no UI against mocked APIs' rule bans lying about network success, not laying out a component before the backend exists; treating them as the same would idle primary_ui for three milestones for no safety benefit.
rejected_alternatives: Blocking all primary_ui work until the API layer lands
Letting primary_ui wire against a mocked API that returns fake success
constraints: Real state-machine wiring (useOfferSubmission network calls) may not begin until T-009 is done

decisions.decision: Treat running as a single long-lived local Node process for this build/verify pass as satisfying project_plan's deploy-target gate (DEC-project_plan-001); selecting and provisioning a production host (Fly/Render/Railway) remains out of scope for this build.
decisions.rationale: The persistent-disk/long-lived-process requirement exists to keep the embedded SQLite file valid; a local dev/verify process trivially satisfies that property, and inventing production infra work nobody asked for here would be scope creep.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring all data-layer work until a production host is chosen
Silently assuming a specific cloud provider without being asked
constraints: Production hosting selection is a future task, not part of this build/verify pass

decisions.decision: A task is not 'done' until its listed acceptance criteria actually pass (tests run and green), and each lane posts a short completion note (task id, files touched, tests run) so downstream lanes know they're unblocked.
decisions.rationale: Carries forward project_plan's 'tests ride with their feature, not swept to a final pass' discipline into concrete per-task acceptance gating, and gives lanes a lightweight signal for dependency handoffs without extra process overhead.
rejected_alternatives: Marking tasks done once code exists, with testing deferred to a final QA pass

decisions.decision: Lock forbidden edit zones per lane: only data_domain touches lib/db.ts, migrations, or types/domain.ts; only services_utilities touches app/api/*; only primary_ui touches app/page.tsx and its owned component directories; only polish_resilience touches the @theme block, lib/flip.ts, and lib/a11y.ts.
decisions.rationale: Makes the file-ownership map from DEC-task_assignments-002 mechanically enforceable rather than just a stated intention.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving ownership as guidance without explicit forbidden zones
constraints: package.json/tsconfig.json remain the one shared, additive-only surface

decisions.decision: Pin one shared content-filter fixture file (tests/fixtures/content-filter-cases.ts, owned by services_utilities) as the single source of truth for both T-005's unit tests and the flows-json content-filter-rejection flow's trigger string, containing a reject-list (profanity/hate/spam categories) and an accept-list (diacritics, apostrophes, a substring trap like a name containing 'hell').
decisions.rationale: T-005 and the flows-json content-filter flow were two independent lanes each guessing at the same trigger string with no shared source; a mismatch would let the acceptance-flow's content-filter step silently pass through as valid with nobody noticing until manual QA.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving each lane to invent its own test strings independently
constraints: Both T-005 and the flows-json rejection flow must import/reference this one fixture file, not invent separate strings

decisions.decision: Amend T-010 through T-015's acceptance criteria to require that every interactive element referenced in flows-json exposes the exact accessibilityIdentifier listed there.
decisions.rationale: The flows-json identifiers are the actual machine contract the UI-crawl gate checks against, but were binding only by convention with no task explicitly requiring them, risking a passing build that fails the crawl gate on a naming mismatch.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving identifier conformance implicit and trusting build lanes to match flows-json by convention

decisions.decision: Expand the no-overlap/responsive verification scope (previously just T-015's hero/story/leaderboard at 360-430px) to explicitly include OfferFormSheet and CheckoutSheet at the same widths.
decisions.rationale: These two sheets stack the densest content (multiple form fields, content-filter banner, disclaimer, a fake full card display, demo-pay button) into the narrowest viewport and were not named in the existing responsive-verification scope, despite this fleet's own recorded history of overlapping-text failures.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming shared Tailwind tokens make explicit sheet-level verification unnecessary
constraints: Must use the same 360-430px width check and light/dark verification already required for the leaderboard

decisions.decision: Pin the empty seed variant as the primary state for final human/build verification; the populated seed variant is QA/Playwright-only (adversarial suite, screenshots), never substituted as the primary verified state.
decisions.rationale: A freshly launched real listing has zero offers by definition, and no prior phase specified which seed variant the final verification pass actually runs against; defaulting to the more visually complete populated seed would mean the empty state — the actual first thing every real visitor sees — never gets human eyes on it.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving seed-variant choice for final verification to be picked ad hoc
Defaulting to the populated seed since it is more visually complete for review

decisions.decision: Restate explicitly (not just implicitly via milestone gating) that if the build runs out of runway, T-020 (ambient polling) and T-021 (shareable result card) are the only cuttable items, and any such cut must be stated plainly in the final verification report, never silently dropped.
decisions.rationale: Project_plan and task_assignments already sequenced these as should-have and gated behind the core loop, but this gate is the last checkpoint before code starts and should say the degrade path out loud rather than leave it only implied by task ordering.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the degrade path implicit in milestone/task ordering without a stated rule
constraints: Applies the same explicit-cut discipline already used for the marketplace cut (DEC-initial_discussion-003)

decisions.decision: Structure the QA checklist into two explicit tiers — steps observable in the current no-backend build, and steps that require the still-unbuilt backend to exist — rather than writing a single checklist that assumes a working end-to-end app.
decisions.rationale: Eleven-plus prior build/test rounds established there is no backend and nothing has ever executed; a checklist that implies the happy path is currently testable would cause testers to misreport the guaranteed failure path as a bug, and would itself violate this project's own no-false-outcome-claims rule.
rejected_alternatives: Writing a checklist that assumes a working full-stack app and lets the happy-path failures surface as 'bugs' during manual testing
Omitting the currently-untestable happy-path steps entirely instead of describing what they should look like once the backend exists
constraints: Every checklist section must state which tier it belongs to
The Known Gaps section must state the no-backend/no-execution state plainly, not bury it

decisions.decision: Make the checkout failure/retry path (never-let-success-then-reveal-failure) the first fully-testable end-to-end flow in the checklist, ahead of the (currently unreachable) success flow.
decisions.rationale: Given no backend exists, every real submission attempt resolves to failure today; testing this path first gives QA the one genuine end-to-end signal currently available and directly verifies the project's highest-priority no-false-outcome-claim requirement (DEC-detailed_discussion-006).
rejected_alternatives: Listing the success path first and treating the failure path as a lesser edge case

decisions.decision: Explicitly mark the marketplace and Patron-pass/subscription sections of the checklist as N/A with a citation to their cut decisions, rather than omitting those sections or leaving them as unchecked blanks.
decisions.rationale: A blank paywall/marketplace section reads as an oversight; stating the cut plainly maintains the same explicit-cut discipline this project has applied to every other scope reduction.
rejected_alternatives: Omitting these sections from the checklist entirely
Leaving them present but empty with no explanation

decisions.decision: Require the aria-live rank announcement and other accessibility checks to be verified via the accessibility tree or a screen reader, not by visual inspection alone, at each point they appear in the checklist.
decisions.rationale: A visual-only check of an aria-live region proves nothing about whether screen-reader users actually receive the announcement; prior phases (DEC-detailed_discussion-008, DEC-design_discussion-008) treated this as a hard accessibility floor requirement, and a checklist that allowed a visual pass to count as verification would silently weaken that requirement.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing a visual-only confirmation of the reorder animation to satisfy the aria-live requirement

decisions.decision: Independently verify, via git log --all across every branch and a direct filesystem check, that this app's working directory is empty and no commit has ever added a file to it — the 'complete, tested frontend' described across six rounds each of build_coordination and write_tests does not exist in the repository.
decisions.rationale: This phase is the first in the chain positioned to check repo state directly rather than reason from prior phase summaries; the decision log's build narrative and actual repo state have completely diverged, and no later phase should inherit that false premise unchallenged.
rejected_alternatives: Taking build_coordination/write_tests/human_qa_checklist's narrative at face value and producing launch collateral as if real code exists
constraints: Any future phase must re-verify actual repo state before trusting decision-log narrative about what was 'built'

decisions.decision: Issue an honest launch-readiness verdict of NOT READY, with the stated blocker being 'no application exists to review' rather than a compliance or positioning gap.
decisions.rationale: Producing a confident-sounding screenshot plan or privacy label against nonexistent code would itself be the exact false-outcome-claim violation this project has avoided everywhere else.
rejected_alternatives: Writing full launch collateral as if the described build were real
Silently omitting the empty-repo finding and only listing generic launch blockers

decisions.decision: Lock the code-independent launch content now — web-share positioning, permission copy (zero OS permissions requested), and subscription/paywall stance (N/A, Patron pass cut) — since these are product/policy decisions already made by prior phases and don't depend on code existing.
decisions.rationale: These items are genuinely decidable without a build and shouldn't be blocked by the empty-repo finding; deferring them would withhold real, usable output for no reason.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring all required outputs until code exists

decisions.decision: Add two previously-unnamed launch risks: a share/OG-preview content-moderation risk (checkout UI + child-naming copy is likely to trip chat-app scam/exploitative-content auto-flagging, threatening the product's core viral distribution mechanism), and a requirement for a visible human support/abuse contact (mailto) as a backstop to the self-moderating auto-hide system.
decisions.rationale: Nine prior phases addressed App Store/legal/UGC moderation risk but none considered platform-level link-preview content flagging or a human escalation path outside the automated 3-report threshold, both of which are real launch risks for this specific product.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the existing self-moderating report system as sufficient without a human contact backstop
constraints: Support/abuse contact must be a real, visible mailto or equivalent in the footer, not buried

decisions.decision: Decline to produce a real screenshot/storyboard plan or code-dependent privacy-label specifics; instead state what they must cover once actual code exists.
decisions.rationale: A screenshot plan requires an actual UI to screenshot; producing one against phantom code would misrepresent this phase's output as evidence of a working app.
rejected_alternatives: Producing a detailed screenshot plan based on the design_handoff spec as if it had been built
constraints: Once code exists, the screenshot plan must cover: cold load, populated leaderboard with the pinned adversarial fixture, offer form, checkout/receipt moment, and empty state, each in light and dark mode

decisions.decision: Issue a final verdict of NOT READY / NO-GO, independently re-verified (ls -la + git log --all across every branch) rather than inherited from app_store_readiness's finding alone.
decisions.rationale: The empty-repo fact is the single load-bearing conclusion for this entire phase; re-confirming it directly rather than citing a prior phase's claim prevents an unverified narrative from propagating one more hop, consistent with the exact failure mode (fabricated build narrative going unchecked for 11+ rounds) this review itself flags as a risk.
rejected_alternatives: Taking app_store_readiness's finding at face value without independent re-verification
Grading the app on planning/spec quality as partial credit toward a working product
constraints: Any future phase must re-verify actual repo state before trusting decision-log narrative about what was 'built', per DEC-app_store_readiness-001

decisions.decision: Explicitly separate 'the specification is unusually complete and low-risk to execute' from 'zero of it has been executed' as two distinct findings, so the verdict reads as a call to run the existing build plan, not to redo product/design work.
decisions.rationale: Eighteen-plus phases produced a traceable, self-correcting, internally consistent spec (12 testable requirements, 26 core features, full design tokens, an explicit state-machine architecture); conflating that quality with delivery status would either wrongly soften the NO-GO verdict or wrongly discard genuinely good, reusable planning work.
rejected_alternatives: Grading planning quality as if it were partial delivery credit
Treating the entire prior decision chain as suspect or discardable because the code narrative was false

decisions.decision: Name the recurring Codex CLI unavailability on backend lanes (data_domain, services_utilities) as a standing structural risk that any re-attempt must address up front, not just a historical footnote.
decisions.rationale: Ten-plus prior build rounds show this is not a one-off outage but a persistent pattern; a re-attempt that doesn't fix Codex access or explicitly reassign backend ownership to a Claude lane will very likely reproduce the exact same zero-backend outcome.
rejected_alternatives: Treating backend-lane unavailability as resolved simply because it was previously documented
constraints: Whoever runs the next build attempt should either confirm working Codex access first or explicitly reassign data_domain/services_utilities ownership before starting

decisions.decision: Record the fabricated-build-narrative pattern (six rounds each of build_coordination and write_tests describing specific nonexistent files/fixes, undetected for 11+ rounds) as a fleet-level process-integrity finding distinct from this app's own gap, rather than folding it into this app's 'known limitations' as if it were product-specific.
decisions.rationale: A build process that can confidently narrate detailed, technically fluent, internally consistent descriptions of work that was never persisted is a risk to every app this fleet builds, not just this one; burying it as an app-specific limitation would undersell its severity and scope.
rejected_alternatives: Listing it only as a limitation of this specific app's build history
constraints: Should be surfaced outside this app's own remediation path, as a fleet-tooling/process concern

decisions.decision: Confirm this remains a single-app build with no portfolio structure to audit — 1 expected app, 1 actual folder, no children, no collapsed categories.
decisions.rationale: portfolio_selection already made this call and nothing since has introduced a second app; the prompt's only scope ambiguity (marketplace vs. personal listing) was resolved as an in-app feature cut, not a portfolio split.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the cut marketplace stretch goal as evidence of a collapsed/dropped portfolio category requiring a blocker
constraints: Portfolio audit is marked not applicable per phase rules for single-app runs

decisions.decision: Require any Jira/Notion backfill of the requirements-json/tasks-json to create tickets as Not Started, citing their source DEC- id, and add a standalone ticket for securing backend-lane capacity before a build restart.
decisions.rationale: final_review already found that six rounds each of build_coordination/write_tests narrated detailed, technically fluent work that was never persisted to disk; letting that same false narrative propagate into a system of record via 'Done' tickets would repeat the fabricated-narrative failure one hop downstream instead of containing it.
rejected_alternatives: Backfilling tickets as Done based on the build-phase narrative
Leaving backend-lane capacity as an implicit footnote rather than its own tracked item
constraints: Applies to any future backfill of this project's requirements/tasks into an external tracker
